sources.content: Proposal HB-305: required two-factor sign-in for Hurnbeck workspace admins. Motivation: in 2026 two admin accounts were taken over with reused passwords, and one attacker exported a full customer list. This proposal makes a second factor mandatory for every account with the Admin or Owner role. Accepted factors are authenticator apps (TOTP) and security keys; SMS codes are not accepted. Admins without a second factor are asked to add one at their next sign-in and cannot reach admin pages until they do.

Rollout and limits. Admins get a 14-day grace period that starts when the proposal ships; during it, a banner reminds them on every visit. After the grace period, the block on admin pages applies. Each account gets 10 single-use recovery codes when it adds a factor. Support can reset a lost factor only after a video identity check. Members without admin roles are not affected. The target ship date is 2027-03-02, and the owner is the Trust and Safety team.

claims.text: Proposal HB-305 does not accept SMS codes as a second factor.
Each Hurnbeck account gets 10 single-use recovery codes when it adds a second factor.
Hurnbeck admins get a 14-day grace period after the two-factor proposal ships.
Under HB-305, Hurnbeck members without admin roles must also add a second factor.
Hurnbeck accepts security keys as a second factor for admins.
Hurnbeck support resets a lost factor only after a video identity check.
